RFC7606-5.1-2.note: Closed 2026-07-20 by plan/spec-rfc7606-5-1-2-relay-shape.md. Origination was already compliant and both splitters emit one NLRI-bearing component per message; what was missing was the RELAY, where an UPDATE that FIT was emitted whole in whatever shape it arrived. Ze is the sender of the bytes it relays, so the restriction applies there too. message.NLRIBearingFieldCount is now the single definition of the count; wireu.WireUpdate.MixesNLRIFields caches the verdict per received UPDATE (the pointer is shared across the per-peer forward loop, so the walk is paid once per message, not once per destination -- measured 3.3ns against 51.7ns, both allocation-free); buildFwdBody splits on shape as well as size in BOTH branches, and Splitter.SplitCompliant is the parsed-side entry point that does the same. A compliant single-field UPDATE still takes the zero-copy append: SplitWireUpdate returns the identical pointer and the reactor hands on the received bytes, asserted by pointer identity rather than equality. Receive -side tolerance (RFC7606-5.1-3) is untouched, and the deliberate MP_UNREACH-first ordering divergence (RFC7606-5.1-1) is unchanged. Evidence: 8 unit tests across three packages, one functional test (test/plugin/rfc7606-relay-one-field.ci, which fails 4/4 when either relay branch is reverted), and 8 mutants killed. 2026-07-20 (interop): a new regression pins that splitting must not MANUFACTURE an RFC 4724 End-of-RIB out of a degenerate empty MP_UNREACH (TestSplitWireUpdateDoesNotManufactureEoR), found by independent review. Interop scenario test/interop/scenarios/47-rfc7606-relay-shape-frr: FRR installs Ze's relayed output; it discriminates a separate duplicate-NEXT_HOP defect on the route-server replay path (FRR rejects the route without the fix). It proves FRR ACCEPTS the Section 5.1 split output but cannot distinguish split from unsplit -- Section 5.1's third bullet obliges every receiver to accept any combination -- so split-vs-unsplit discrimination stays in the unit tests and the .ci. 2026-07-29 (plan/spec-rfcgate-2-evidence.md): test/plugin/rfc7606-relay-one-field.ci now carries the `RFC requirement:` tag and appears in the fingerprint below. Nothing about the test changed; it was cited as evidence in this very note while the ledger still showed this MUST NOT as unit-only, because nobody had tagged it. .ci was already an admissible carrier -- this was a missing binding, not a missing capability. Verdict unchanged. 2026-07-29 (plan/spec-rfcgate-3-audit-teeth.md): the recorded value was `implemented`, which is outside the four values ai/skills/ze-rfc-audit.md defines, so no legal verdict had ever been recorded here and there was nothing to preserve. RE-JUDGED against rfc/full/rfc7606.txt Section 5.1 second bullet ('An UPDATE message MUST NOT contain more than one of the following: non-empty Withdrawn Routes field, non-empty Network Layer Reachability Information field, MP_REACH_NLRI attribute, and MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute') rather than mapped mechanically, because rewriting the word without reading would fabricate a judgement nobody reached. Verdict: enforced. The tests assert the RFC's own quantity -- NLRIBearingFieldCount over all ten combinations, then <=1 per emitted message -- not a proxy for it; each of the three sender-side entry points has a fixture that guards BOTH that the input already FITS (so only shape can force the split) and that it starts non-compliant, so the assertion cannot pass for the wrong reason; the negatives use genuinely compliant single-field inputs and assert POINTER IDENTITY of the passed-through bytes, which an equal-but-copied payload would fail, so the pair discriminates rather than wearing two hats; and the split is asserted to preserve every route, so a compliant-but-lossy split fails too. Would-it-fail is recorded from mutation, not inferred: reverting either relay branch leaves one message where the test requires several, and the .ci fails 4/4 with message-mismatch. 2026-08-01 (RE-JUDGED, not re-stamped): the tagged unit TestForwardSplitsMixedShapeAcrossContextsThatFits changed in 8e67a9b03, which took the RFC 6793 transcode buffer from the read pool. Read the commit diff rather than the edit's own claim about itself: the only change to that function is `defer ReturnReadBuffer(result.transcodeBuf)` plus a comment. No assertion, guard, fixture or tag text moved, and the other nine tagged units are byte-identical (only this unit sha and the enclosing file sha differ from the previous record). Re-read RFC 7606 Section 5.1's second bullet in rfc/full/rfc7606.txt and all ten tagged tests. Three independent reasons the pool release cannot weaken the proof. First, a `defer` runs after every assertion, so no assertion outcome can depend on it. Second, the updates this test reads come from fwdSplitParsedUpdate, which copies each section into a fresh slice, so they do not alias transcodeBuf at all and returning it cannot disturb what the loop reads. Third, ReturnReadBuffer is a no-op on a zero handle (reactor/session.go:142), so the line is safe when no transcode ran. The assertion still counts the RFC's own quantity, NLRIBearingFieldCount <= 1 on each emitted UPDATE, over a fixture guarded to FIT so only shape can force the split, and it still requires more than one emitted UPDATE, which is the assertion that dies if the MixesNLRIFields condition is removed from either arm. Verdict unchanged: enforced.

RFC7606-5.1-3.note: {single-polarity} positive is honest: a MUST-accept obligation has no conforming rejection. rfc7606_test.go:583 (TestRFC7606MPReachIPv4NextHopValid) places MP_REACH after ORIGIN and AS_PATH (not first) and asserts ActionNone. Ze has no receive-side ordering check, so it accepts any position; if an ordering check were added that rejected non-first MP, this would fail. Caveat: proves the 'any position' clause but not the 'combination' clause. 2026-07-29 (plan/spec-rfcgate-2-evidence.md): the caveat above -- 'proves the any position clause but not the combination clause' -- is now closed by TWO bindings at the wire altitude, both landed. (1) test/plugin/rfc7606-relay-one-field.ci sends ONE UPDATE mixing Withdrawn Routes with NLRI and asserts the source peer is neither reset nor answered with a NOTIFICATION; it runs inside ze-verify on every push. (2) Interop scenario 47-rfc7606-relay-shape-frr drives the same shape from a raw injector at a real FRR and is now tagged. An earlier revision of THIS note said scenario 47 was not tagged because it failed at an unrelated assertion, attributed to the adj-rib-in replay path prepending Ze's AS while the forward path did not. That attribution was WRONG and is withdrawn: there is ONE prepend gate (reactor_api_forward.go:711, `facts.isEBGP && !facts.rsClient`) and both rails reach it; facts.rsClient is populated only from the session/rs-client leaf, which defaults to false and which no interop scenario set. Ze was correctly prepending for a peer that was, as configured, a plain eBGP peer. Setting rs-client in ze.conf -- what RFC 7947 route-server semantics require of a route server's clients -- turns the scenario GREEN; scenario 14-route-server-frr was red for the identical reason and is fixed the same way. §5.1's second bullet forbids a SENDER to emit that shape, so no conforming peer daemon can drive it and an injector is the only carrier that can. The two bindings are not interchangeable: the .ci is merge-gate evidence, the interop scenario is nightly and advisory. Verdict unchanged.

RFC7606-5.4-1.note: Closed 2026-08-01 by plan/spec-fixit-rfc7606-5-4-discard-unrecognized-nlri.md, reversing the {gap} recorded here on 2026-07-20. Thomas was re-asked on 2026-08-01 with the full counter-argument in front of him and chose full compliance; the earlier ruling was void twice over (ai/rules/rfc-compliance.md voided every answer pointing away from full compliance on 2026-07-27). JUDGEMENT. The requirement has two clauses and both are tagged. Positive: an EVPN UPDATE mixing route types ze implements with type 99 loses only the unrecognized one, asserted as the exact surviving byte sequence, with the action asserted RFC7606ActionNone so no OTHER rule can have produced the result (question 3, isolation). Negative: bgp-ls/bgp-ls keeps an unknown NLRI type 99 in place and unchanged, which is RFC 9552 Section 5.2's own MUST -- 'this document deviates from the default handling behavior specified by Section 5.4 (paragraph 2) of [RFC7606] for Link-State address family' -- and is the escape clause the requirement's own text names. The two polarities are different inputs with opposite expected outcomes, not one assertion wearing two hats. WOULD IT FAIL (question 2): mutation-verified at both tiers on 2026-08-01. Making applyTypedNLRIDiscard an early return flipped 3 of the 6 unit tests RED and flipped test/plugin/rfc7606-54-discard-unrecognized-nlri.ci RED with the receiver's wire carrying 6304DEADBEEF; the bgp-ls file correctly stayed green, because it asserts the behaviour that already existed. WHY THE PROOF IS AT THE RELAY (question 1, what the RFC says rather than what the code does): 5.4 discards a ROUTE, which means neither installing nor propagating it. The RIB is not the propagation gate -- reactorForwardRS (internal/component/bgp/reactor/forward_rs.go) fans the RECEIVED wire to every eligible peer with no RIB event involved, and buildFwdBody (internal/component/bgp/reactor/forward_body.go) appends peerWire.Payload() verbatim on the same-context path -- so a RIB-level test would have passed while ze went on relaying the route. The discard is therefore in enforceRFC7606 (internal/component/bgp/reactor/session_validation.go), upstream of both consumers, and the functional tags assert on the second peer's wire. The per-family ruling is registry-driven (internal/core/bgp/nlri/nlritype), registered by the plugin owning the family, so no central package names a family and a family nobody has ruled on discards nothing.

RFC7606-6-1.note: IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-20. Session.rfc7606Diagnostics (reactor/session_validation.go) logs the NLRI involved (withdrawn and announced IPv4 prefixes, decoded ADD-PATH-aware) and the entire UPDATE body as hex, wired into all three RFC 7606 outcomes: attribute-discard, treat-as-withdraw (logged BEFORE SynthesizeWithdraw rewrites the body, so the dump is what the peer sent) and session-reset. TestRFC7606DiagnosticsListNLRIAndUpdate asserts the prefix and the raw ORIGIN bytes appear; TestRFC7606DiagnosticsCoverSessionReset covers the reset path; TestIPv4PrefixListTolerance pins the decoder on malformed input. The negative is TestRFC7606DiagnosticsCostsNothingWhenDisabled, which asserts zero allocations when the level is off -- that is what pins the Enabled() guard, since slog evaluates arguments eagerly and without the guard a peer could make ze hex-encode every malformed UPDATE it sends. TestRFC7606DiagnosticsSilentWhenDebugDisabled sits alongside it but only shows no line is emitted; a level-filtering handler drops the line with or without the guard, so it does NOT pin it. Note the requirement's 'must' is lowercase in the RFC and so outside RFC 2119; kept at MUST level as a ze policy choice.

RFC7606-8-1.no_code_path: RFC 7606 Section 8 binds the AUTHORS of future BGP attribute specifications: 'A document that specifies a new BGP attribute MUST provide specifics regarding what constitutes an error for that attribute and how that error is to be handled.' It is an obligation on a document, discharged by writing one, so no running implementation can either satisfy or violate it and there is no code path in Ze to point a test at. Distinct from a gap: a gap is behaviour Ze could implement and does not.
RFC7606-8-1.note: {not-applicable} annotation holds up: RFC §8 ('A document that specifies a new BGP attribute MUST provide specifics regarding what constitutes an error...') binds AUTHORS of future BGP attribute specifications, not a running implementation. There is genuinely no Ze code path that could satisfy or violate it, so it is not implementable (per the method, an implementable N/A would be 'wrong' -- this one is not). Recorded 'enforced' only in the sense that the N/A classification is honest and correct; there is no test to demand and no finding. 2026-07-29 (plan/spec-rfcgate-3-audit-teeth.md, owner ruling OR-1): the value was `enforced` with an empty `tests` map, which the schema now refuses -- `enforced` means the tests would fail if the code stopped complying, and this note itself says there is no test to demand. That was the honest reading of a vocabulary with no honest state for it, so Thomas added one rather than have the record re-judged: `not-applicable`, which requires an empty `tests` map, a mandatory `no_code_path` reason, and an independently committed {not-applicable} annotation on the checklist line. No judgement changed here; the same finding is now recorded in a word that means it. UNRESOLVED and deliberately left so: ai/rules/rfc-compliance.md voids {not-applicable} as AUTHORITY, so the annotation this verdict agrees with is itself a classification the owner has voided. This ruling makes the VERDICT honest about what the code does; it does not re-affirm the annotation, and re-deriving that is fleet-drain work under the rfcgate umbrella's D4. RFC7606-8-1 needs looking at again when the drain reaches it.
